title: Distinguish transformer families, pretraining and adaptation, inference context, and sparse-expert routing without equating fluent output with verified reasoning

questions.prompt: A team serves a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model across several GPUs. Requests arrive one at a time (batch size 1). The MoE model turns out slower per token than a dense model that has about the same number of **active parameters per token**. Which explanation best fits this result?
options: At small batch sizes the router falls back to activating every expert, so the MoE model performs the full dense arithmetic of all its experts for each token.
Every token still multiplies through the model's total parameter set, so the active-parameter count understates the arithmetic actually performed per token.
Active parameters only approximate part of the arithmetic. The MoE model also pays for router work, cross-device token dispatch and load imbalance, which small batches expose.
Small batches make the serving layer switch between separate model checkpoints for each request, and loading those checkpoints adds per-token latency.

rubric.point: Selects the option attributing the slowdown to routing, cross-device dispatch and load imbalance that active-parameter counts do not capture.

questions.model:
**Active parameters only approximate part of the arithmetic. The MoE model also pays for router work, cross-device token dispatch and load imbalance, which small batches expose.**

Optional: Sparse routing still activates only top-k experts, and total parameters affect storage and placement, not per-token arithmetic. MoE routing is inside one model, unrelated to application-level model routing.

questions.prompt: A developer wants a chatbot that writes free-form replies, and plans to use a pretrained BERT checkpoint as the model that generates the reply text. Explain why BERT, on its own, is unsuitable for generating these open-ended replies. Address both (a) what BERT's architecture outputs and (b) what its pretraining objective trains it to do.

rubric.point: (a) Architecture: states that BERT is encoder-only, producing contextual representations (per-token or pooled vectors) for a task head, with no autoregressive decoder that emits new tokens one at a time.

(b) Pretraining: states that BERT is pretrained to predict masked tokens using context on both sides (bidirectional), not causal next-token prediction, so its pretraining does not directly train continuing text.

questions.model:
(a) BERT is encoder-only: it turns input into contextual vectors for a task head and has no autoregressive decoder to emit a continuation token by token.

(b) It is pretrained with bidirectional attention to predict masked tokens from both sides, not with a causal mask on next-token prediction, so its pretraining does not directly train causal next-token continuation.

Optional: a decoder-only (GPT-style) or encoder-decoder model fits generation.

c2.text: Bert is a classifier model, where it generetes decisions and probability, not a free form text. It possbile to use bert to select pre-existing text based on its classification

annotations.quote: Bert is a classifier model, where it generetes decisions and probability
annotations.note: BERT is an encoder-only model that outputs contextual vectors for a task head. It is not inherently a classifier, and the answer never says it lacks an autoregressive decoder that emits tokens one at a time.
This correctly says BERT does not produce free-form text. It gives no architectural reason, such as the missing decoder.

annotations.quote: It possbile to use bert to select pre-existing text based on its classification
annotations.note: Using BERT to pick or rank existing responses is a valid selection use. It does not answer why BERT cannot generate.
Part (b) is absent. You need to say BERT is pretrained to predict masked tokens using context on both sides, not to predict the next token.

c2.feedback: You reached the right conclusion that BERT isn't suited to free-form generation, but you gave neither the encoder-only architecture nor the masked-token pretraining objective.
